scope: Targeted round-3 community candidates for ACR106 / ACR008 / ACR009 / ACR010. Non-GitHub sources only (LangChain Forum, Stack Overflow, public blogs/gists). Excludes all cases already used in evals/realworld and evals/realworld2.

sources_attempted.method: Discourse public search.json + /raw/<topic>/<post>; queries: cache_policy, cache key, retry_policy, retry loop, node executed twice, one value per step, self loop, resume, debug
StackExchange API 2.3 tagged=langgraph (cache, InMemoryCache, retry_policy, resume, interrupt, one value per step, subgraph retry) + questions?filter=withbody

sources_attempted.detail: web_fetch to www.reddit.com / old.reddit.com resolves to a non-public IP in this environment; web_search returned no public Reddit results. No login/paywall bypass attempted.

sources_attempted.method: web_search for debug trace, node_start/node_end, replay-safe HITL, retry tracing
sources_attempted.detail: Several tracing/replay-safety writeups were found, but none exposed a raw resume/replay event sequence or a citable trace file; one raw ADR fetch timed out and no public gist with a LangGraph resume trace was located.

ACR106.note: No public non-GitHub post with a resume/replay-marked debug trace was found. One Stack Overflow post contains an actual checkpoint-history event sequence, but it demonstrates update_state/time-travel behavior, not a completed node being restarted after resume.

ACR008.note: CachePolicy / cache-key material found, but none shows the ACR008 contract: cache_policy on a callable object / lambda / partial / unresolved parameter, with shared cache or an identity-collision consequence.

ACR009.note: retry_policy material found, but no post shows a retried node invoking two or more subgraphs with a checkpoint-namespace consequence.

ACR010.note: Only an adjacent duplicate-execution case (conditional edge plus plain edge) was found; it is not a self-loop and its state key has a reducer. #2336 is excluded as already used.

recommendations.forum-2964: Closest ACR106 material: resume after interrupt re-runs agent_node and produces a second AIMessage; includes graph/node code plus a detailed debug narrative, though no raw trace.
recommendations.forum-2456: Closest ACR010-adjacent material: a complete runnable graph where conditional and plain edges make fanin execute twice; not a self-loop and the affected key has a reducer, so it can only be a near-miss / fixture seed.
recommendations.forum-1283: Complete runnable cache example (CachePolicy on a named node + InMemoryCache + InMemorySaver) where caching silently stops; tests cache/checkpointer interaction rather than callable identity.

selection_note: This is a targeted capability search, not a prevalence sample. Candidates marked target_fit=near_miss are kept for fixture planning but do not satisfy the protocol's exact target definitions; they must not be counted as real validation samples.

candidates.title: Twice execution of agent when using the interrupt
candidates.summary: After resuming an interrupt, the agent node produces two AI messages: the OP's debug narrative describes the resumed run entering agent_node, re-entering interrupt_node, then starting agent_node again from the top. Graph and node code are included.
candidates.notes: Closest ACR106 material: explicit resume-reported duplicate execution. No raw trace/debug stream or node_start/node_end events were attached, so has_trace=false; needs a fixture or trace instrumentation before ACR106 can be judged.

candidates.title: Can we resume from the checkpoint and continue running at the interruption point instead of starting from the first node?
candidates.summary: A checkpoint is saved at B and C fails, but restarting with the stored checkpoint_id still starts at A instead of resuming near B/C; the OP prints the restored checkpoint id but sees no continuation. LangGraph 0.6.5.
candidates.notes: Resume/checkpoint near-miss; no duplicate-completed-node trace, no raw node events. Includes config/code snippet but not a minimal graph.

candidates.title: Refreshing event stream using langchain/react use stream replays old checkpoints
candidates.summary: On reconnect/first subscribe, a self-hosted LangGraph server replays buffered protocol events; the client re-applies old values snapshots and replays terminal lifecycle events. The OP instrumented the wire (583 protocol events, 0 checkpoint events, 14 pauses / 6 resumes) but attached no raw trace file.
candidates.notes: Event-replay near-miss: useful for understanding protocol-level replay and why UI state rewinds, but not an ACR106 resume trace. The instrumentation metrics are in prose, not an event log, so has_trace=false.

candidates.title: Debug issues during node transitions
candidates.summary: A graph exits without running an expected next node; enabling set_debug(True) and set_verbose(True) produced no useful clue, and the OP asks what conditions can stop node execution and how to debug it.
candidates.notes: Documents the absence of usable debug/trace output for a node-transition failure. No code, no trace; this is a material-limitation candidate, not a validation sample.

candidates.title: LangGraph resume after interrupt is not working properly when running with more than 1 worker in uvicorn
candidates.summary: Resume after an interrupt works with one uvicorn worker but returns a 500 ('query') with four workers; includes graph construction, MemorySaver and a custom interrupt tool. Deployment/worker-concurrency symptom.
candidates.notes: Resume near-miss: points at process-local checkpointer/worker state, not at replaying a completed node. No trace or event sequence.

candidates.title: Langgraph `update_state` modifies unexpected fields
candidates.summary: A complete runnable example prints the checkpoint history twice around update_state, including checkpoint ids, parent ids and state values; the second update unexpectedly carries node2 values while as_node says node1.
candidates.notes: Only candidate with an actual event/checkpoint sequence (has_trace=true), but the sequence is update_state/time-travel history, not a resume of a completed node. It is useful as a trace-format reference for acr trace, not as an ACR106 resume sample.

candidates.title: InMemoryCache usage conditions and potential incompatibility with InMemorySaver
candidates.summary: With a complete runnable example, adding an InMemorySaver makes an InMemoryCache node cache stop working; CachePolicy is attached to a normal named function, and the OP asks about cache/checkpointer invocation conditions.
candidates.notes: CachePolicy + shared cache material, but not ACR008's callable-identity contract (the callable is a module-level function with stable identity). Useful for cache/checkpointer interaction, not for validating ACR008.

candidates.title: Re-execute / restart from a specific task in a functional API
candidates.summary: Functional-API restart/caching discussion; a reply notes that key_func only receives task input args (no thread_id/run_id), so cache-run identity must be passed as task arguments.
candidates.notes: Cache-key identity/scope near-miss (key_func args), not the ACR008 callable-object/lambda/partial identity case. No failing repro or code in the OP.

candidates.title: Does the cache param do anything when using create_agent?
candidates.summary: Asks whether compile(cache=...) applies to tool nodes created by create_agent, since the user cannot attach CachePolicy to those internal tool nodes.
candidates.notes: Cache-policy exposure question; no callable identity and no failure trace. Not an ACR008 sample.

candidates.title: Gracefully handling GraphRecursionError from subgraphs so the parent agent can retry or degrade
candidates.summary: A parent create_agent delegates to a subgraph; when the subgraph exceeds recursion_limit it raises GraphRecursionError, and the OP asks how to retry/degrade and whether per-subgraph limits can be set. Includes create_agent/middleware configuration.
candidates.notes: Parent retry + subgraph near-miss, but uses GraphRecursionError and manual retry, not retry_policy on a node invoking 2+ subgraphs. No multi-subgraph checkpoint-namespace symptom.

candidates.title: Parallel Nodes: how to manage failures or exceptions
candidates.summary: Q&A about failure handling for parallel nodes; a reply shows retry_policy on nodes plus try/except fallbacks and Send fan-out error handling.
candidates.notes: retry_policy material, but nodes invoke APIs, not multiple subgraphs. It is guidance, not a failure report, and cannot validate ACR009.

candidates.title: The best way in LangGraph to control flow after retries exhausted
candidates.summary: Asks how to redirect flow when a retriable node exhausts attempts; the answer explains RetryPolicy has no exhaustion hook and shows manual retry / Command.goto / conditional-edge patterns.
candidates.notes: Retry-semantics near-miss with code, but no subgraph invocation and no checkpoint namespace symptom. Not an ACR009 sample.

candidates.title: Duplicate node execution when using conditionals
candidates.summary: A conditional edge fan-out plus a plain edge makes the fanin node execute twice when a preparation node is enabled; complete runnable example.
candidates.notes: Execution-duplication near-miss, but the duplicated execution comes from conditional + plain edges, not a self-loop; the affected keys use an operator.add reducer. It does not satisfy ACR010 and must not be counted as a validated sample.
